spec_match.rationale: Demonstrates the source-ladder pattern the feature exists to serve, and proves the type-attribute skip with resource-timing evidence rather than assertion.

interactive.rationale: Ladder select re-renders rung verdicts and markup; the build-the-element button constructs a real <audio> with real <source> children and reports which URLs the browser actually fetched.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Blurb promises watching which rung this browser lands on, decided by its own answers — delivered, including the honest currentSrc correction note.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers the no-playable-rung case, the all-404 fall-through behaviour of currentSrc, and a wrongly-skipped-sources check in the measurement itself.

references.rationale: ChromeStatus link plus the HTML media-load-algorithm spec link.

conformance.rationale: Feature suite passes 6/6 here; the a-source-type-decides-before-any-request assertion matches this page's fetch-evidence design.

runtime_evidence.rationale: On this Chromium 153 the first (IAMF) rung is chosen (probably) — the real support path; the intentional 404 fetches are documented in-page and behave as described.

telemetry_health.rationale: type-attribute-skipped-fetches is a real falsifiable assert, but the deliberate 404 source fetches also generate resource-error telemetry on every button press, which will look like failures in the telemetry triage view despite being the demo's documented mechanism.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables, rung states colour-coded with AA-safe pairs, markup block scrolls.

accessibility.rationale: Select and button labelled, outputs aria-live, 11/12 tab stops with visible focus (the audio element supplies its own internals).

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Measured 52px of unintended horizontal page overflow at 360×740 DPR3: the .rung grid (2.5ch 1fr auto) with white-space:nowrap on .state pushes the stage to ~412px, dragging the heading, select and output with it.

openQuestions.title: Fix the 52px mobile overflow in the ladder rungs
openQuestions.detail: At 360px the .rung rows overflow the viewport (measured right edge 412px; every element in the first stage section stretches with them). The nowrap .state span plus the auto grid column is the culprit. Smallest fix: allow .state to wrap on narrow viewports (e.g. white-space:normal under a 480px media query) or give the grid minmax(0,1fr) and let the row wrap to two lines. This is the only parity defect on the feature.

openQuestions.title: Keep expected 404 telemetry distinguishable from real failures
openQuestions.detail: The build-the-element probe intentionally fetches three nonexistent /media/… URLs, producing console 404s and resource.error telemetry every run. Consider marking these expected (e.g. an in-page note is present, but telemetry has no such flag) or asserting the expected count so triage can separate them from genuine resource regressions.

summary: Verified on headless Chromium 153 (Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12) driven over CDP via a Playwright script — chrome-devtools-mcp is unavailable in this cloud environment; desktop 1280×800 and mobile 360×740 DPR3 full-page screenshots captured and inspected. The demo's fetch-evidence design is excellent and the IAMF rung is genuinely chosen on this 153 build, but the rung grid overflows a 360px viewport by 52px — the one real defect found on this feature — and the intentional 404s will read as resource errors in telemetry triage.
